quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on film study after the Golden State loss
quotes.excerpt: A lot of that was individual film. So you break it down with guys individually on their assignments.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: Following your comments from the other night, I had a question about just how you approach film after facing Golden State with such little time. I know you want to draw home some lessons, but you also have to move forward and tonight's opponent. How do you approach that?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: A lot of that was individual film. So you break it down with guys individually on their assignments, shot quality, transition defense, the things that they did well that we could have taken away, but also some of the high-quality shots that they did make, but then our offense that allowed them to get out in transition to get some of those easy baskets.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on his post-loss film process: We break it down with guys individually on their assignments, shot quality, and transition defense to see what we could have taken away.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains how he reviews film with his players individually following a recent loss to the Golden State Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Importance of starting the five-game homestand with a win
quotes.excerpt: It's huge. The way that we respond back from the other night is going to be big.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: As far as tonight goes, the start of a five-game homestand, how critical is this stretch and important to setting the tone tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: It's huge. The way that we respond back from the other night is going to be big. Our fan support being at home, playing the right way, the right style of basketball. Again, we've said it before, making every game a dogfight, and that's what we've got to continue to do starting tonight on the homestand.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the team needs to make every game a dogfight as they kick off a five-game homestand tonight.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the importance of starting a five-game homestand with a win after a recent loss.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Addressing the lack of turnovers and deflections on the road
quotes.excerpt: Playing Golden State, that was the one that you really stands out the most.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Staying on the film theme, getting turnovers and deflections and points off turnovers has been a really big key to your team in the first 10 games. We really didn't see that on the road trip. Did you see anything on film as to why not?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: Playing Golden State, that was the one that you really stands out the most is like the way that they move and cut and play without the basketball. There's not a lot of dribbling, there's not a lot of pick-and-roll. It's more playing through Draymond, which was finding off-ball actions with Steph. And so being able to get deflections there and get a hand on the basketball and is usually a lot of pick-and-roll stuff, weak-side defense coming over and we were slow in a lot of those areas as is. But they also play a different style of basketball that doesn't always have that as an option to really get out on the break to get steals from them.

quotes.social_post: Mosley explains the difficulty of getting deflections against the Warriors: They play a different style of basketball that doesn't always have that as an option.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains why his team struggled to generate deflections and turnovers against the unique offensive style of the Golden State Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Explaining Derrick Quinn's injury and bench behavior
quotes.excerpt: Derrick had been talking about his neck prior to the game, and so in that moment, he had gone to walk back to go get his neck treated.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Going back to the Golden State game, can you share some light on the Derrick Quinn situation?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: I mean, we've seen it, we've all looked at it. And the thing about that was Derrick had been talking about his neck prior to the game, and so in that moment, he had gone to walk back to go get his neck treated on because he was going to lay down and didn't want to lay down on the bench and that's a trickier arena to find the locker room and it was either walk right behind our bench which as this closed off, there's a lot of people there, so he just not the path we wanted him to take and it does not a good not a good optic, but that was the reason for him walking that way to get back to the locker room to go get some treatment on his neck.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley addresses the Derrick Quinn situation, clarifying that the player was walking to the locker room for neck treatment: It was not a good optic, but that was the reason for him walking that way.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley clarifies why Derrick Quinn walked behind the bench during the game against Golden State due to a neck injury.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mosley on the biggest adjustment as a first-year head coach
quotes.excerpt: You can't give me a team that doesn't have somebody down. You can't give me a team that doesn't have a big out, a guard out.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Everybody comes in with a plan, you talked about it media day, but after 10 games, just what's been your biggest adjustment as a coach in New Orleans?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: That's the league. You can't give me a team that doesn't have somebody down. You can't give me a team that doesn't have a big out, a guard out. The injuries are part of the league. You just find a way to adjust. There's no major adjustment that you're going to make. You just plug in the next person and then we talk about doing it by committee. So adjustments are made every single game. There's no that's the biggest piece that we've continued to do is that whatever lineup we're able to put out there, we're going to put out there and the style of play that we want to play. Again, I'm going back to it, it's got to be a physical, gritty game for us night in and night out.

quotes.social_post: After 10 games as head coach, Jamahl Mosley says the biggest adjustment is managing constant injuries: You just plug in the next person and talk about doing it by committee.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley reflects on his first ten games as head coach and the necessity of adjusting to player injuries.
